content.title: Denver vs. Wisconsin Final Score, Highlights: Pioneers Win 11th National Championship with Stunning Comeback | NESN
content.text: If you purchase a product or register for an account through one of the links on our site, we may receive compensation. Learn more > Through two periods at T-Mobile Arena, Denver looked dead in the water. Stifled by an unrelenting Wisconsin forecheck, the Pioneers managed just five shots in the first 40 minutes of Saturday's national championship game. But their championship pedigree surfaced in the final frame, allowing David Carle's squad to author a comeback for the ages in Las Vegas.Denver scored two goals in the third period to stun Wisconsin and claim an 11th national title, the most in NCAA history. Freshman goaltender Johnny Hicks once again proved to be a steadying force for the Pioneers, making 29 saves in a 2-1 victory. The Pioneers have now won three national championships in the last five seasons under Carle (2022, 2024 and 2026).Check out all of the highlights from the national championship thriller.Denver vs. Wisconsin score 123FDenver0022Wisconsin1001Denver vs. Wisconsin live updates, highlights from 2026 NCAA championship game(All times Eastern)Final: Denver 2, Wisconsin 18:05 p.m.: The Denver Pioneers have won their 11th national title.After looking completely dead for 40 minutes, the Pioneers' championship pedigree came alive in the third. Two goals in the final frame and another masterclass from Johnny Hicks flipped the script.8:04 p.m.: With 28 seconds left, Wisconsin ices the puck, and Hauser has to come off the bench.8:03 p.m.: Wisconsin will have an offensive zone faceoff with 46 seconds left.7:58 p.m.: The extra attacker is on for Wisconsin. With 1:50 remaining, the Badgers need a goal.7:57 p.m.: A flurry of chances for the Pioneers, but Hauser makes three consecutive saves to keep Wisconsin alive.7:52 p.m.: Wisconsin had a chance to tie the game, but a shot rattles off the post. Plenty of fans in the arena thought we had a tie game.Then, the Badgers are whistled for holding. It's a brutal penalty with 4:14 remaining.7:48 p.m.: GOAL! Denver has taken the lead. After a period of sustained zone time, Kyle Chyzowski gets a tip on a shot from the point right in front of Hauser, who did not have a stick.7:48 p.m.: There's under six minutes left. Could we get another overtime period?7:35 p.m.: Hicks sprawls out to make a spectacular save on a shot that would have given Wisconsin the lead. The crowd roars for the goaltender, who has kept the Pioneers in the game despite the shot margin.7:33 p.m.: GOAL! Rieger Lorenz gets Denver started on the forecheck, then a Kristian Epperson pass to Garrett Brown sets up a one-timer. That shot is saved, but Lorenz is there to tuck in the rebound.7:28 p.m.: The Pioneers finally enjoy some time in the offensive zone before Wisconsin gets a 2-on-1 chance. Jack Horbach rips a shot, but Hicks stands tall.7:20 p.m.: It's time for the third period in Las Vegas.End of the second period: Wisconsin 1, Denver 07:06 p.m.: In the last minute of the second period, Denver has its best sustained zone time. It results in one shot on goal and a few opportunities that miss the net.Still, Wisconsin takes a 1-0 lead into the locker room.6:59 p.m.: A puck is thrown right in front of Hauser, but Denver still can't get a shot off. On the other side, Hicks sees a shot the whole way and covers it up.6:54 p.m.: The Wisconsin defense simply isn't allowing Denver to create any opportunities around the net.6:43 p.m.: The Badgers get a shot from the point, but Hicks swallows it up. Wisconsin is outshooting Denver, 15-4.6:41 p.m.: Denver finally gets some shots on goal, but Hauser is there to make the saves.6:36 p.m.: Denver has not yet registered a shot seven minutes into the second period.6:26 p.m.: The puck has dropped in the second period. The Badgers win the first faceoff.End of the first period: Wisconsin 1, Denver 06:09 p.m.: The Badgers have a 1-0 lead after outshooting the Pioneers in the first period, 10-2.6:08 p.m.: As the period is winding down, the Badgers keep on pressing. A shot from Aiden Dubinsky is saved by Hicks.6 p.m.: GOAL! Wisconsin strikes first in the national championship with Vasily Zelenov ripping a shot from the left circle past Hicks.5:58 p.m.: Hicks handles every shot thrown at him, and both teams are now 0-for-1 on the power play.5:53 p.m.: Wisconsin has limited Denver's high-octane offense to only two shots, and now, it will go to the power play for the first time today. Cale Ashcroft goes to the box for Denver (boarding).5:52 p.m.: Denver's first shot of the game comes eight minutes in. Daniel Hauser makes a pad save on a Sam Harris shot.5:45 p.m.: We're at the 14:10 mark, and it's time for the first commercial break.5:41 p.m.: Wisconsin gets an odd-man rush on the power play, but Gavin Morrissey's shot is saved by Hicks. The Badgers have killed the power play.5:38 p.m.: Denver will be the first team with a man advantage. Wisconsin's Oliver Tulk is going to the box for tripping.5:37 p.m.: The first quality chance goes to Wisconsin, which gets a clear shot from the point, but Johnny Hicks makes the save.5:34 p.m.: The puck has dropped, and we are underway in Las Vegas.5:30 p.m.: Teams are on the ice, and the start of the national championship game is moments away.5:21 p.m.: On the other side we have the Pioneers, who are looking for their NCAA-leading 11th championship.5:16 p.m.: The official lines are out for the Badgers.5 p.m.: The start of the 2026 national championship game is only 30 minutes away.4:39 p.m.: Both teams have arrived at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.4:30 p.m.: Welcome to the national championship game. Either Denver or Wisconsin will be the king of the 2025-26 college hockey season.How to watch Denver vs. Wisconsin tonight: TV channel, live streamTV channel: ESPNLive stream: ESPN app, fuboDenver vs. Wisconsin will air nationally on ESPN.
